entries.title: Public voting: see what you have voted on, undo a vote, step through the ballot
entries.summary: submissions a voter has scored carry a **Voted** badge, the ballot counts them (*3 of 12 voted*) and filters to **Voted** or **Not voted**; inside a submission, **Previous** and **Next** move through the ballot and **Back to all submissions** returns to the list, as evaluators do in their queue. A voted submission shows its saved score, and **Undo vote** takes it back while the round is open, returning the vote to a **Votes per voter** budget. Works on event, Interest Form and awards rounds.

where.path: Public voting ballot on the Site (event, Interest Form and awards rounds)

entries.use_case: Voters see what they have already voted on, can undo while the round is open, and step through the ballot like evaluators do — fewer abandoned ballots and fewer 'did my vote count' emails.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers planning a community vote; anyone who had voter confusion last cycle.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events and awards programs with public voting.

entries.title: Sites: favicon and social share image
entries.summary: **Branding** on a Site gains a **Favicon**, shown in the browser tab on every page of the Site including vote ballots, and a **Social share image**, the card shown when a link to the Site or a vote link is pasted into Slack, LinkedIn, Teams or iMessage. Both offer **Upload** or **Copy from…** the organization's image library, and both are carried over when a Site is copied. Left empty, the favicon falls back to the logo and the share card to the portal background image or logo.

enable.path: Site → Branding → Favicon and Social share image

entries.use_case: A vote link or Site pasted into Slack, LinkedIn or Teams now shows the customer's own card and tab icon instead of Sessionboard's, which matters for every public-facing vote and program site.

cs_action.note: Customers with a live Site should set both before they share links.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Site launch, public voting launch, any branding review.
internal.gotchas: Falls back to the logo / portal background when empty. Carried over on Site copy.

entries.title: Email subsession speakers from a session selection
entries.summary: the Send Email composer in **Sessions** gains **Sessions to include**: keep the default **Selected sessions only**, add every selected session's subsessions with **Selected sessions and their subsessions**, or send to **Subsessions only**. It works with **Select all N matching this filter**, so one send reaches every subsession presenter in a program, each with their own subsession's merge tags.

where.path: Sessions → select → Send Email → Sessions to include

entries.use_case: Abstract programs put presenters on subsessions. One send now reaches every subsession presenter with their own subsession merge tags, instead of exporting and re-importing lists.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Any customer using subsessions / abstract sessions who emails presenters.

entries.title: Upload slots: ask speakers for specific files
entries.summary: **Program → Settings → Files** gains a **File Requests** card with a **Use upload slots** switch. On, you define a list of slots — Poster, Presentation, Handout — each with its own due date and extended deadline, accepted file types, file count, **Required** flag, session filters (**Format is Poster**, say) and the roles who may upload; drag to reorder, archive and restore. Turning it on converts your current due date, file limit and file types into the first slot, so nothing changes for speakers until you add more. New and cloned events start with slots on; existing events keep their single file request until you flip the switch. The Poster Gallery page flags events still on the single request, since a gallery collects from a Poster slot.

enable.path: Program → Settings → Files → File Requests → Use upload slots

entries.use_case: Ask speakers for a Poster, a Presentation and a Handout as separate requests, each with its own deadline, file types and session filter — instead of one generic file request the organizer has to sort afterwards. Poster Gallery collects from the Poster slot.

cs_action.note: Turning it on converts the existing single request into the first slot; new and cloned events start with slots on. Walk existing events through it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Speaker-readiness planning, poster sessions, Poster Gallery onboarding.
internal.gotchas: Existing events keep the single request until the switch is flipped; Poster Gallery flags events still on the single request.

entries.title: Public voting on Interest Form evaluation plans reaches voters
entries.summary: the **Public voting** banner on an Interest Form round now links to the organization Site that lists the form (it previously offered to create an event Site), voters following that link land on their ballot, and the round's results table loads. Eligible-voter lists and ticket-holder weighting remain event-only, so Interest Form rounds no longer show a **Who can vote** group.

where.path: CRM → Interest Forms → Evaluations → round → Public voting banner

entries.use_case: Public voting on an Interest Form round now actually reaches voters through the organization Site; results load.

internal.when_to_bring_up: CRM customers running year-round community votes on interest forms.
internal.gotchas: Eligible-voter lists and ticket-holder weighting stay event-only.

entries.title: Voting on an Interest Form ballot
entries.summary: Format, Level and other catalog dropdowns on a submission now show their labels to voters instead of internal ids; a saved score stays on the scorecard after **Submit score**; and a score chosen before signing in is submitted automatically once the voter is back from the sign-in link, provided the scorecard still asks the same questions. The sign-in email a voter receives says *Sign in to cast your vote* rather than talking about submissions, and the sign-in and welcome cards fall back to readable text when a Site's saved text colour cannot be read on its primary colour.
entries.use_case: Voters see readable labels instead of ids, scores survive sign-in, and the sign-in email talks about voting.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Only if a CRM customer reports ballot oddities.
